BACKGROUND The Organization Grounded Solutions Network (GSN) is the nation’s largest network of practitioners and advocates dedicated to expanding shared equity models and other innovative approaches that keep housing affordable for generations. GSN’s work is guided by a clear and powerful vision: a future where everyone has access to an affordable home in a community that supports health, education, economic opportunity, and long-term well-being. As a national membership organization, Grounded Solutions equips the people advancing this work every day—including nonprofit and government practitioners, community resident leaders, advocates, elected officials, and housing professionals—with the tools, knowledge, and support they need to thrive. GSN advances the creation and preservation of high-quality, permanently affordable housing and center racial equity in every aspect of the work. Grounded Solutions’ membership is comprised of funders, land trusts, housing developers, and other groups across the US. Staff provide technical assistance and policy guidance on the local, state and national levels. Programs include Homes for the Future and HomeKeeper, as well as creative financing and investment partnerships. To continue Grounded Solutions’ impact and to support the growing number of investments, Grounded Solutions seeks a Senior Vice President, Impact Investment to develop financial partnerships that will support Grounded Solutions’ mission and grow its assets. The Position The Senior Vice President of Impact Investment will lead Grounded Solutions’ strategy for securing and deploying significant capital in ways that create real, measurable impact — socially, environmentally, and financially. The SVP will own the full investment lifecycle: sourcing, underwriting, structuring, closing, and ongoing portfolio management across debt, equity, and blended-finance instruments. Partnering closely with the executive team, board, and external capital partners (banks, foundations, government agencies, institutional investors), the SVP will grow Grounded Solutions’ assets under management, strengthen the organization’s impact, and increase the portfolio to enable Grounded Solutions to support future work and investments. Solutions Network Innovative Finance, LLC subsidiary, on multi-year acquisition fund strategy, capital sources, and long-term stewardship risk Be a visible, credible voice for GSN with investors, members’ and partners’ capacity to put capital to work Capital Raising and Investor Relations Secure low-cost loans and program-related investments that support portfolio growth goals Structure and layer the capital needed for strategic acquisitions and dispositions of single-family homes across multiple national markets Set thoughtful investment policies, underwriting standards, and risk parameters with credit/risk committees, accounting for the unique risk profile of affordable home assets (like rental or sales price restrictions) Lead capital raising efforts — CDFI capital, foundation grants, program-related investments, and federal, state, and local government sources — to fund acquisition and program needs Steward an increasingly diverse capital stack to balance strategic goals with smart risk management and strong balance sheet outcomes Keep internal fund management, liquidity, and capitalization strategies sound, with a high standard of care and prudent risk management Build and nurture relationships with private banking, investment portfolio managers, and partners Support the Grounded Solutions Network Innovative Finance, LLC subsidiary Board of affordability preservation, homeowner wealth-building outcomes, portfolio retention, and resale/foreclosure trends across the home portfolio Track the metrics that matter most for long-term affordability — units preserved in perpetuity, AMI levels served, and homeowner equity accrued versus market appreciation foregone Ensure impact data shapes subsidy structuring decisions and is reported clearly and credibly to funders, public agency partners, and the board Team and Operations Build, lead, and mentor a talented team spanning acquisition/underwriting and investment portfolio stewardship Institute the policies, procedures, and systems (including investment portfolio management software) needed to scale acquisition and long-term monitoring Oversee the budget and financial Fund requirements, fair housing/fair lending laws, state shared equity statutes, funder-specific affordability covenants) Ensure future ground lease terms and resale formulas are compliant with funder requirements (HOME, CDBG, CDFI lenders, state trust fund covenants) over multi-decade terms Prepare for and present at meetings of the investment/credit committee and board of directors Qualifications 15+ years of experience in financial investment management, community development finance, banking, or a related field, with a track record of taking on progressively senior responsibility Deep knowledge of debt/equity structuring, underwriting, and portfolio risk management A proven track record of closing complex transactions and raising capital from institutional or philanthropic sources Hands-on experience with shared equity homeownership models — community land trusts, limited equity co-ops, or deed-restricted programs Strong knowledge of affordable housing capital sources (Philanthropic Program Related Investments and grants, U.S. Dept. of Treasury CDFI Fund loans, HUD grant programs like HOME and CDBG, state/local trust funds, and LIHTC-adjacent tax credit structures where applicable), plus a solid grasp of impact measurement frameworks and mission-driven finance A bachelor’s degree is required; an MBA, CFA, or related advanced degree is a plus Additional Experience Relevant financial transaction experience with community land trusts, community development corporations, or shared equity housing nonprofit intermediaries Familiarity with Grounded transactions Existing relationships with public housing agencies, impact investors, or philanthropic organizations directing capital toward affordable homeownership outcomes What Will Help You Thrive Excellent written and verbal communication, including presenting confidently to boards, investment committees, and public funders WHO WE ARE Work Environment The Grounded Solutions team works out of Washington, DC, and the preferred location for the SVP is the DMV area. review_candidates.title: Postdoctoral Researcher in Global Health Economics – BEACON-HD at EUR
review_candidates.company: Medical Delta Living Lab Better In Better Out
review_candidates.description: Introduction BEACON-HD is an international, Horizon Europe-funded research project testing two promising strategies — telemedicine with self-monitoring and community-based medication delivery — to strengthen primary health care systems and improve the management of hypertension and type 2 diabetes in rural Rwanda and Uganda. As a postdoctoral researcher, you will play a leading role in the economic and equity analyses within this large-scale field experiment, working closely with an international consortium of health economists, clinicians and implementation scientists. Join us to help generate the evidence needed to make chronic disease care more effective, efficient and fair in low-resource settings. Job Description Are you interested in leading applied research within a large-scale field experiment aimed at improving the management of chronic disease in low-resource settings? Do you want to help make healthcare delivery more effective, efficient and equitable for people living with hypertension and diabetes in Sub-Saharan Africa? We offer a post-Doc opportunity for 36 months (90% research, 10% teaching) within BEACON-HD, a large EU Horizon Europe-funded international consortium project. BEACON-HD is testing two promising implementation strategies, telemedicine with self-monitoring and community-based medication delivery, through a large-scale field experiment in rural Rwanda and Uganda. The project combines this field experiment with qualitative, behavioral and economic research to understand not only whether these strategies work, but how, for whom, and at what cost. Responsibilities As a postdoctoral researcher, you will take a leading role in the economic and equity work package, working closely with the project's PI and the wider consortium. Your responsibilities will include: Contributing to and helping coordinate the BEACON-HD field experiment, from the design of data collection instruments to implementation, analysis and interpretation of results, in close collaboration with consortium partners across Europe, Rwanda and Uganda. Leading the collection, quality assurance and analysis of data on costs, resource use and outcomes together with our in-country partners, including field visits to Rwanda and/or Uganda. Building and extending a decision-analytic (Markov) model to estimate the cost-effectiveness of telemedicine with self-monitoring and community medication delivery, relative to standard care, from the perspective of the public health systems in both countries. Leading a budget-impact analysis assessing the short- and medium-term financial implications of scaling up these strategies. Leading an equity-modelling study evaluating how the implementation strategies affect health outcomes across socioeconomic subgroups, and their potential to contribute to universal health coverage. Co-authoring peer-reviewed publications and presenting findings at international conferences. Contributing to the day-to-day coordination of the work package This postdoc position combines field-based data collection and analysis with decision-analytic modelling and applied econometric work. It offers the opportunity to generate new methodological and empirical insights into the evaluation of health-system-strengthening strategies, helping to guide fairer and more efficient healthcare policy in low- and middle-income countries. You can view the full job vacancy here. Application deadline: 9 October 2026
